Saritha Kulkarni., Hcgp For R6) This Writ Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226 & 227 Of The Constitution Of India Praying To Issue Writ Of Certiorari Or Any Other Appropriate Writs Or Directions Quashing The Impugned Notice Dated 07/10/2023 Bearing No.A.Y/Raranv/P.R/183/2023-24 Issued By R4 Vide Annexure-E And Etc. This Writ Petition, Coming On For Further Hearing, This Day, The Court Made The Following: Order 1.
texts.facts: Issue writ of Certiorari or any appropriate writs or directions setting aside the rejection order dated 28.10.2023 bearing application No. N232419101163534 passed by the Health Officer (zonal)/Respondent No.5 vide Annexure-G produced along with this application. 2. The petitioner claims to be engaged in the business of owning and operating cloud kitchens under brand name "Sharief Bhai" as regards which the petitioner has obtained licenses from the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India. The petitioner took on lease the ground floor of the premises bearing No.45 and 46 of Channa Sandra Village, Uttarahalli Hobli, Bangalore South Taluk-560061 measuring 1950 Sq.ft. for the purpose of running his business. A trade license for the said business having been applied for on 17.12.2022, Respondent No.5 on 7.10.2023 called upon the petitioner to vacate the premises, since the petitioner was using the basement parking as a kitchen. It is in that background that the petitioner had approached this Court seeking for the aforesaid reliefs. NC: 2024:KHC:3742 3. The standing counsel was directed to accept the notice for respondent on 12.10.2023. On 13.12.2023, a submission was made that the application filed by the petitioner had been rejected on the ground that in the basement a kitchen was being run. Hence, the counsel for the petitioner submitted that no such kitchen is being run but only certain items were stored and an affidavit of undertaking would be filed by the petitioner that the basement was not be used for any such purpose, such an affidavit came to be filed on 25.10.2023. 4. Subsequently, the application filed by the petitioner allegedly came to be rejected on the grounds that the property is in a residential area. Hence, an amendment was carried out challenging the same, objections were also filed by the respondent. 5. Initially it was contended by the corporation that the road width in front of the property of the petitioner was NC: 2024:KHC:3742 less than 40 feet and as such the no commercial activity could be carried out therein. Subsequently, it was contended that no permission from the fire forces had been obtained. In that view of the matter the Karnataka State Fire and Emergency Service Department represented by the Director General of Police and Director General of Fire and Emergency Services was brought on record as party respondent, since the BBMP was not in a position to place on record as to under what provision and what permission is required to be obtained. 6. A report came to be filed enclosing notification dated 20.9.1971 by the learned AGA on behalf of the Fire Department. It was categorically stated that there is no permission which is required from the Fire Department except that certain of the guidelines were required to be followed by a restaurant. Maltesh Paitl vs Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike on 29 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70981554/ 3 NC: 2024:KHC:3742 7. On that day, on instructions another submission was made by the learned counsel for respondent that the width of the road was less than 40 feet. Hence, the respondent was directed to carry out an inspection measure of the road in front of the property of the petitioner and file a report. The report to that effect has been filed along with a memo dated 19.1.2024 which now indicates that the road width is 21.20 mts. i.e., 70 feet and plot size is 464.69 sq. mtr. with a construction of five floors put up thereon. 8. Sri. Sathayananda., learned counsel for BBMP would now submit that it is only 30% of the built up area which could be used for commercial purpose, since the property of the petitioner lies in ring 3 whereas the entire property has been used for commercial purpose. On enquiry as to why the width of the road has changed from time to time i.e., on first occasion it was submitted that the road width was less than 40 feet in so far as the petitioner in WP No.23065/2023 it has been NC: 2024:KHC:3742 submitted that the road width is 70 feet in so far as another petitioner in WP No.28108/2023 the road width is stated to be 19.40 mts. there is no particular explanation which is offered more so when both the property lie on the same road.
